thread:
sara: Heads-up — planned maintenance on runtime GPU pool (us-west) Thu 02:00–04:00 UTC. We'll pin model versions + drain in-flight requests. Need a short statuspage update and a customer email template. Any concerns?

michael: +1 on pinning. Recommend pin to v1.12.3 for all hosted routes and set automatic fallback to cpu-small for non-critical traffic.

emma: Can we avoid customer-visible rate limits? If we pause autoscale there might be transient 429s. Suggest adding note about brief degraded throughput.

sara: good call. We'll add a line. Also: ops will do canary drain 30 mins prior and cutover window 02:30–03:15 for highest-risk clusters.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled by @michael at 2026-03-26T02:00:00Z — action: maintenance/2026-03-26/runtime-gpu. Status: scheduled.

linda: Drafting statuspage + email now. Posting quick snippets below, feel free to tweak.

linda: STATUSPAGE SNIPPET (short):
"2026-03-26 02:00 UTC — Planned maintenance on runtime GPU pool in us-west. We will pin model versions and perform kernel updates. Customers may see brief increases in latency or reduced throughput between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. No expected data loss. For questions contact support@redwood.ai"

linda: EMAIL TEMPLATE (subject + body):
Subject: Planned maintenance — runtime GPU pool (Mar 26, 02:00–04:00 UTC)

Hi <Customer>,

We will perform planned maintenance on our runtime GPU pool in us-west on Mar 26 from 02:00–04:00 UTC. The maintenance includes model version pinning and kernel updates to improve stability. During the window you may experience brief periods of increased latency or reduced throughput; the service should remain available.

What we are doing:
- Pinning model versions (v1.12.3) and enabling automatic fallback for non-critical routes
- Draining in-flight requests with a 30-minute canary period
- Applying kernel and driver updates

Potential impact:
- Short latency spikes or rate-limit responses (429) for heavy workloads
- No data loss is expected

If you have workloads that cannot tolerate interruptions, reply and we can coordinate a private maintenance window or provide options on Dedicated/Private deployments.

Thanks,
Redwood Support

michael: I suggest adding an ops-runbook link for post-maint checks. lmk if linda can paste the runbook URL.

linda: Pasted runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/maintenance/runtime-gpu-checks (internal)

emma: For release notes, call out the kernel version and the quantization patch. Also log the pin reason: "avoiding regression from new kernel optimizations" — helps audits.

sara: OK — I'll merge snippets and queue an email send for 01:00 UTC day-of. @deploy-bot please trigger a pre-maint webhook 1h prior to window so support gets an automated reminder.

deploy-bot: pre-maint webhook scheduled for 2026-03-26T01:00:00Z — targets: #support, #eng-oncall.

michael: Approved. If canary shows >5% error increase we rollback pin and open an incident.

sara: noted. I'll add the rollback trigger language to the statuspage update and the ops checklist. :white_check_mark:

linda: Final draft uploaded to /shared/comm-drafts/2026-03-26-gpu-maintenance.md

emma: Thanks everyone. I'll be on call for the first hour.

sara: Closing thread — publishing updates to statuspage and scheduling the email. Ping here for any last-minute edits. :wave:
